name: Guyana
description: Guyana is rapidly emerging as an attractive destination for expats, driven by its booming oil and gas economy and status as the only English-speaking country in South America. It offers a unique blend of Caribbean culture and abundant natural beauty, from dense rainforests to cascading waterfalls, alongside increasing job opportunities.
longdescription:
Life in Guyana for expats is marked by a dynamic economy, largely fueled by significant offshore oil discoveries since 2015, which has transformed the nation into one of the world's fastest-growing economies and a high-income country by the World Bank's classification. [27, 41] This economic boom is attracting professionals, particularly in engineering, project management, and offshore operations, although it has also led to a rising cost of living, especially in housing and dining in the capital, Georgetown. [36, 31]

Culturally, Guyana offers a rich tapestry of influences, blending Indian, African, European, and Caribbean traditions, with English as the official language and Guyanese Creole widely spoken. [2, 22, 29, 38] Expats can immerse themselves in diverse social activities, from religious festivals to community events, and enjoy an array of Indian, African, Chinese, and Amerindian-inspired dishes. [34, 37, 39] While the country boasts incredible scenery and outdoor adventure opportunities, safety remains a concern, particularly with high crime rates in certain areas of Georgetown. [2, 17, 21, 26, 32] Expats often opt for private healthcare facilities for a higher standard of care and should secure comprehensive health insurance. [37]

visas.name: Guyana Work Permit
visas.description: Work permit for foreign nationals employed in Guyana. The booming oil sector is driving high demand for skilled workers in engineering, finance, and energy.

extra_info:
### Visas & Notes
- Work permit required for foreign employment
- Oil sector booming — skilled workers in high demand
- English-speaking, making integration straightforward

Citizenship by Descent.desc: Citizenship by descent is available to individuals born abroad on or after May 26, 1966, if at least one parent was a Guyanese citizen at the time of their birth. [3, 14, 23, 24, 33, 35] The Guyanese parent's name must be recorded on the foreign birth certificate. [33, 35] Registration can typically be done at a Guyanese consulate or embassy. [14, 35]

Naturalization.desc: Foreign nationals can apply for naturalization after residing legally in Guyana for a specified period. Generally, this requires continuous legal residence in Guyana for at least seven years, demonstrating good character, an intention to reside permanently, and competence in the English language. [3, 7, 14, 18] Commonwealth citizens or citizens of the Republic of Ireland may register as Guyanese citizens after five years of residence. [3, 18] The process involves applying to the Minister responsible for immigration, undergoing background checks, and taking an Oath of Allegiance. [3, 7, 14, 40]

Birthright.desc: Anyone born in Guyana automatically acquires citizenship by birth (jus soli), with minor exceptions for children born to diplomatic personnel or enemy aliens. [3, 7, 14, 23, 24] This principle applies to individuals born on or after the commencement of the 1980 Constitution.

Spouse and Family.desc: A foreign national married to a Guyanese citizen is eligible to register for citizenship. [3, 7, 14, 18, 23, 24] Requirements include a legal and valid marriage, proof of a genuine relationship and cohabitation, good character, police clearance certificates, and financial stability. [7, 12, 14] While historically applications could be made soon after marriage, there are ongoing discussions (as of early 2024) to consider new criteria, such as a requirement for couples to live together for one year before applying, to prevent marriages of convenience. [28] The application process involves submitting documents to the Ministry of Home Affairs and an interview with the Immigration Department. [12]

tax_advice:
*   **Personal Income Tax (PIT):** Residents are taxed on worldwide income, while non-residents are taxed only on Guyanese-source income. [19, 20, 25]
    *   Income tax is charged at a rate of 28% on the first GYD 2,040,000 of chargeable income annually, and 40% on the balance. [19]
    *   Alternatively, other sources indicate 28% on income less than GYD 1,800,000 and 40% on income in excess of GYD 1,800,000, with a personal deduction of GYD 780,000 or one-third of annual income, whichever is greater. [5, 6, 11]
    *   For non-residents, a flat 20% rate applies to Guyanese-source income. [11]
    *   The tax year aligns with the calendar year (January 1st to December 31st), and individual tax returns are typically due by April 30th of the following year. [19]
*   **Corporate Income Tax (CIT):**
    *   Commercial companies (deriving at least 75% of gross income from goods not manufactured by them, or engaged in telecommunication, banking, or insurance) are taxed at 40%. [4, 6, 8, 16]
    *   Non-commercial activities are taxed at 25%. [4, 6, 16]
    *   Telephone companies are taxed at 45%. [5, 6, 16]
    *   A Minimum Corporation Tax (MCT) of 2% of turnover applies to commercial companies if it's higher than the 40% or 45% chargeable profits tax. [5, 8, 16]
*   **Value Added Tax (VAT):** The standard VAT rate is 14% on the taxable supply of goods and services. [5, 9, 10, 15]
    *   Certain goods and services are zero-rated (e.g., exports, some medical supplies) or exempt (e.g., educational services, residential rent, financial services). [9, 15]
    *   Mandatory registration for VAT applies if taxable activities exceed GYD 15,000,000. [5, 9, 15]
*   **Withholding Tax (WHT):**
    *   WHT is generally levied on payments to residents and non-residents, with rates varying by type of payment (e.g., dividends, interest, royalties). [4, 5, 6, 19]
    *   A 10% WHT applies to payments on contracts to non-resident companies. [5, 6, 16]
    *   Branch profit net of corporation tax is subject to 20% withholding tax. [5, 6, 16]
*   **Capital Gains Tax:** A 20% tax is imposed on net chargeable gains derived from the disposal of capital assets. [5, 6, 15, 19] Exemptions exist for private residences if proceeds are reinvested in another primary residence. [15]
*   **Social Security Contributions (NIS):** Compulsory contributions are required for both employees (5.6% of insurable earnings) and employers (8.4% of insurable earnings) up to a monthly earning threshold of GYD 280,000. [5, 9, 15, 19]
local_tips:
*   **Cost of Living:** Be prepared for a higher cost of living, particularly in housing and some consumer goods, as the oil boom has led to significant price increases, especially in Georgetown. [36]
*   **Language:** While English is the official language, learning some Guyanese Creole can enhance local interactions. [2, 22, 29, 38]
*   **Safety:** Exercise a high degree of caution due to prevalent crime, including petty crime and violent crime. Avoid walking alone after dark, especially in certain areas of Georgetown (e.g., Tiger Bay, Albouystown, Stabroek Market, Botanical Gardens, Agricola, Buxton). [2, 17, 21, 26, 32]
*   **Transportation:** Public minibuses are often overcrowded and unsafe; taxis are generally safer but choose trusted drivers. Driving requires a Guyanese Driver's Permit, which can be obtained after converting an International Driving Permit. [21, 26, 32]
*   **Registration:** For long-term stays, securing appropriate visas and work permits is crucial; employers typically handle the work permit application process. [31]
*   **Healthcare:** Consider private healthcare facilities for better standards and shorter wait times, and secure comprehensive health insurance. [37]
*   **Cultural Integration:** Engage in local events and communities to experience the diverse culture and build relationships. [34, 37, 39]
